terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, intransitive, with a predicate adjective or noun
evidence: Cic. Div. 2.108: sī quandō aliquod somnium vērum ēvāserit
terms.comment: Of how a thing turns out (vērum, vānum), and of what a person becomes: perfectus Epicūrius ēvāserat (Cic. Brut. 131).

evidence: Caes. BC 3.104.1: ex amīcīs inimīcī exsistunt

phrases.latin: sī quandō aliquod somnium vērum ēvāserit
phrases.english: if ever some dream has turned out true

phrases.latin: vereor, nē haec quoque laetitia luxuriet nōbīs ac vāna ēvādat
phrases.english: I fear that this joy too may run riot with us and prove empty

phrases.latin: ut plērumque in calamitāte ex amīcīs inimīcī exsistunt
phrases.english: as friends so often turn out enemies in misfortune

sources: Lewis & Short: evado · Lewis & Short: exsisto
Cicero (Div. 2.108, Brut. 131), Livy (23.12.12) and Caesar (BC 3.104.1) checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).
